LESSON: WATER HARDNESS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.3: Water hardness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Water hardness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the importance of different types of water?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the physical properties of water
2. apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life
3. appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life
4. identify external and internal parts of a leaf
5. explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis
6. describe the process of photosynthesis
7. appreciate the process of photosynthesis in nature

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER HARDNESS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water hardness helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Describe the physical properties of water

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the physical properties of water. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the physical properties of water.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water hardness” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the physical properties of water. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Water hardness matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Water hardness this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify external and internal parts of a leaf

What this means
In this part you learn to identify external and internal parts of a leaf. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify external and internal parts of a leaf.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify external and internal parts of a leaf. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis

What this means
In this part you learn to explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Water hardness matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain adaptations of the leaf to photosynthesis. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Describe the process of photosynthesis

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the process of photosynthesis. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the process of photosynthesis.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Water hardness this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the process of photosynthesis. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water hardness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water hardness” around your school. (skill: describe the physical properties of water)

Example 2: Say why Water hardness matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Water hardness this week. (skill: appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Water hardness” around your school. (skill: identify external and internal parts of a leaf)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water hardness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the physical properties of water.
3. Practise this skill: apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the applications of soft and hard water in day-to-day life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Water hardness from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water hardness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Water hardness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the importance of different types of water?
2. Why is hard water preferred for drinking?
3. What is the importance of photosynthesis in nature?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water hardness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the physical properties of water.
5. Be able to: apply methods of softening hard water in day-to-day life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
